subject: Clarify SOC 2 scope: Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC (audit period gap & bridge evidence)
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@greenfield.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: audits@acmefin.com
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 applicability for our deployment mix + bridge letter request

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare for our vendor review I need a quick clarification on Redwood's SOC 2 Type II applicability across hosting modes. Our technical architecture will use a mix: most traffic to the hosted endpoint, some steady-state traffic pinned to a Dedicated pool starting 2028-06-01, and a small set of batch jobs running in our VPC-connected private deployment.

Specific asks:
- Which environments are covered under Redwood's last Type II report (period: 2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31)?
- For Dedicated pools that started serving our traffic after 2028-06-01, can we get a bridge letter or attestation covering the gap between the Type II window and the time the Dedicated environment entered service?
- We also need to understand whether cross-pool routing/fallback behavior could cause hosted-mode tokens to be processed in Dedicated or private pools (this affects scope). If so, what evidence do you provide to demonstrate tenant isolation and routing policies?

If easier, a short mapping of artifacts (SOC 2 report, bridge letter, tenant mapping CSV, KMS/HSM attestation, network diagram) to the specific hosting modes would be ideal. Our auditors are timeboxed and appreciate a succinct packet.

Best,
Sara Lim
VP, Vendor Risk & Compliance
Greenfield Financial

---
Attachment: vendor_compliance_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@greenfield.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 applicability for our deployment mix + bridge letter request

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (Compliance) and Dylan (Platform) to provide the artifact mapping and a draft bridge letter. Karthik Iyer (CC not added yet) will weigh in on routing behaviour and tenant isolation for Dedicated pools.

Quick answers up front:
- Our published Type II report (attached) covers the hosted control plane and hosted inference endpoints that were in production during the 2027 audit window.
- Dedicated pools that were provisioned after the audit window are not covered by that Type II. We can issue a bridge letter that documents controls alignment, sampling methodology, and a list of evidence items for the gap period — provided we can confirm the Dedicated pool configuration and activation date.
- Cross-pool routing: there are two important modes to consider — controlled failover (configured by customer policy) and automatic regional fallback. Both can be configured to avoid tenant co-mingling; we'll describe policy-level routing and provide tenant-mapping and routing-flow artifacts.

We'll prepare:
1) Draft bridge letter (language for auditors)
2) Tenant mapping CSV showing which tenant IDs are pinned to Dedicated pools and dates of activation
3) Routing flow diagram and a short description of fallback policies
4) KMS/HSM attestation excerpt and encryption keys handling notes for VPC/private deployments
5) A short statement on sampling and observability (what logs/traces you can request)

Kimberly/Dylan: can you confirm we can share the SOC 2 PDF (already uploaded to Drive), the tenant mapping export, and the two supporting diagrams? Also, if practical, please add Karthik on the routing explanation.

Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear context. I pulled together the initial artifact mapping and a short FAQ below; attached are the SOC 2 PDF and a tenant mapping CSV export. Also attached: a PNG with the routing-fallback flow and an editable bridge-letter-draft.

Artifact mapping (summary):
- SOC 2 Type II (2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31): covers Redwood hosted control plane and hosted inference endpoints as of those dates. It does not cover Dedicated or Private deployments provisioned after the audit window. (Attachment: SOC2-Type-II-2027.pdf)
- Bridge letter: we can provide a customer-specific bridge letter that: 1) states alignment of controls for Dedicated/VPC components where controls are equivalent, 2) calls out differences (e.g., customer-managed network controls for private deployments), and 3) lists evidence items you can request. (Attachment: bridge-letter-draft.docx)
- Tenant mapping: tenant_mapping_dedicated_vs_vpc.csv lists tenant IDs, pool assignments, activation dates and a short note on isolation (logical v. physical).
- Routing and fallback: routing-fallback-flow.png shows how requests are routed by policy and where automatic fallback may occur; policies enforce that pinned tenants do not get routed to other tenants' Dedicated pools unless explicitly configured.
- KMS/HSM: for Private/VPC we provide a key-handling attestation (excerpt included in the bridge letter); for Dedicated we run customer keys in our KMS with separation via key policies and role-based access control.

Two clarifying questions before we finalize the bridge letter:
1) Can you confirm the earliest timestamp you consider in-scope for the Dedicated pool? You mentioned 2028-06-01 — is that the activation date you want represented?
2) Do your auditors require explicit listing of any automatic regional fallback behavior (we can include or redact depending on sensitivity)?

Security notes (brief):
- Pinned Dedicated pools are logically isolated and backed by tenant mapping exported from our control plane; physical co-tenancy is possible only in dedicated-gpu pool sharing scenarios we do not use for pinned deployments.
- Network egress paths for VPC/private deployments are customer-managed; we will include diagrams and a short KMS attestation showing where encryption-at-rest and key ownership differ.

If that aligns, we'll update the bridge letter draft and provide a signed PDF.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly — that's very helpful. To answer your questions:
- Yes, 2028-06-01 is the activation date we'd expect on the bridge letter.
- Please include a short description of automatic regional fallback behavior (we don't need low-level routing tables; a paragraph describing triggers and safeguards is fine).

A couple of additional asks from our auditors:
1) Can you include an explicit statement about whether inference KV cache or prefix caching could cause hosted-mode requests to be material to Dedicated pools during failover? If so, we need mitigation language in the bridge letter.
2) For KMS: please confirm whether keys are customer-managed in the VPC offering and whether Redwood performs any key-escrow or key-rotation on behalf of customers for Dedicated pools.

If you can share the finalized bridge letter (PDF, signed) and a small packet (SOC2 PDF + tenant mapping + routing PNG + KMS attestation) by EOD Friday we'll be in good shape for our auditor kickoff next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — feel free to call if that's easier.

Best,
Sara Lim
VP, Vendor Risk & Compliance
Greenfield Financial
